//go:build js && wasm

package client

import (
 "math"
 "syscall/js"
)

// checkedJSFailure deliberately contains no foreign exception or property name.
// In particular, js.Error.Error itself reads an untrusted message property.
// Callers may recover/format this fixed Go value without inspecting that object.
type checkedJSFailure struct{}
func (checkedJSFailure) Error() string { return "nextgo: native operation failed" }

// The only bare property reads in this helper are this one-time capture. This
// assumes ordinary trusted initial globals and native built-ins when the Go
// package initializes. It is not a hostile-global/prototype sandbox or a check
// of native branding. The captured values are never replaced by target reads.
var checkedJSReflection = func() struct { get, set, apply, construct, defineProperty, create, array, object js.Value } {
 global := js.Global()
 reflection := global.Get("Reflect")
 object := global.Get("Object")
 return struct { get, set, apply, construct, defineProperty, create, array, object js.Value }{
  get:reflection.Get("get"), set:reflection.Get("set"),
  apply:reflection.Get("apply"), construct:reflection.Get("construct"),
  defineProperty:reflection.Get("defineProperty"), create:object.Get("create"),
  array:global.Get("Array"), object:object,
 }
}()

func checkedJSRecover() {
 if recover()!=nil { panic(checkedJSFailure{}) }
}

// checkedJSPrimitive is intentionally not a recursive ValueOf replacement.
// Explicit builders make aggregate construction visible to the caller's byte,
// arity, lifetime and authority checks. No helper admits work or storage.
func checkedJSPrimitive(value any) js.Value {
 defer checkedJSRecover()
 switch value:=value.(type) {
 case js.Value:return value
 case js.Func:return value.Value
 case nil, bool, string,
  int, int8, int16, int32, int64,
  uint, uint8, uint16, uint32, uint64, uintptr,
  float32, float64:
  return js.ValueOf(value)
 default:panic(checkedJSFailure{})
 }
}

func checkedJSGet(value js.Value, property string) js.Value {
 defer checkedJSRecover()
 return checkedJSReflection.get.Invoke(value,property)
}
func checkedJSSet(value js.Value, property string, next any) {
 defer checkedJSRecover()
 nextValue:=checkedJSPrimitive(next)
 result:=checkedJSReflection.set.Invoke(value,property,nextValue)
 if result.Type()!=js.TypeBoolean || !result.Bool() { panic(checkedJSFailure{}) }
}
func checkedJSIndex(value js.Value, index int) js.Value {
 defer checkedJSRecover()
 if index<0 { panic(checkedJSFailure{}) }
 return checkedJSReflection.get.Invoke(value,index)
}
func checkedJSLength(value js.Value) int {
 defer checkedJSRecover()
 length:=checkedJSReflection.get.Invoke(value,"length")
 if length.Type()!=js.TypeNumber { panic(checkedJSFailure{}) }
 n:=length.Float()
 const maxSafeInteger=9007199254740991
 if math.IsNaN(n)||math.IsInf(n,0)||n<0||n!=math.Trunc(n)||n>maxSafeInteger||n>float64(int(^uint(0)>>1)) { panic(checkedJSFailure{}) }
 return int(n)
}

// checkedJSDefineData creates its descriptor without a recursive builder.
// The captured native Object.create(null) returns a fresh, unexposed ordinary
// null-prototype object. Reflect.set on that descriptor therefore cannot reach
// an inherited setter. Only fixed own data fields are installed before the
// descriptor is passed to captured Reflect.defineProperty. The target's
// inherited setters are never used for the new data entry.
func checkedJSDefineData(target js.Value, property any, value js.Value) {
 defer checkedJSRecover()
 var key js.Value
 switch property:=property.(type){
 case string:key=js.ValueOf(property)
 case int:
  if property<0{panic(checkedJSFailure{})}
  key=js.ValueOf(property)
 default:panic(checkedJSFailure{})
 }
 descriptor:=checkedJSReflection.create.Invoke(js.Null())
 if descriptor.Type()!=js.TypeObject { panic(checkedJSFailure{}) }
 for _,field:=range []struct{key string;value js.Value}{
  {"value",value},
  {"writable",js.ValueOf(true)},
  {"enumerable",js.ValueOf(true)},
  {"configurable",js.ValueOf(true)},
 }{
  result:=checkedJSReflection.set.Invoke(descriptor,field.key,field.value)
  if result.Type()!=js.TypeBoolean||!result.Bool(){panic(checkedJSFailure{})}
 }
 // property is supplied only by the builders as a Go string/nonnegative int.
 // No Go aggregate reaches Invoke conversion on this path.
 result:=checkedJSReflection.defineProperty.Invoke(target,key,descriptor)
 if result.Type()!=js.TypeBoolean||!result.Bool(){panic(checkedJSFailure{})}
}

// checkedJSArray accepts only primitive values, js.Value and js.Func. A nested
// array/object must first be constructed explicitly by the respective helper.
// These finite inputs still need the caller's existing precharge and limits.
func checkedJSArray(values []any) js.Value {
 defer checkedJSRecover()
 prepared:=make([]js.Value,len(values))
 for i,value:=range values { prepared[i]=checkedJSPrimitive(value) }
 array:=checkedJSReflection.array.New(len(prepared))
 for i,value:=range prepared { checkedJSDefineData(array,i,value) }
 return array
}
func checkedJSObject(values map[string]any) js.Value {
 defer checkedJSRecover()
 prepared:=make(map[string]js.Value,len(values))
 for key,value:=range values { prepared[key]=checkedJSPrimitive(value) }
 object:=checkedJSReflection.object.New()
 for key,value:=range prepared { checkedJSDefineData(object,key,value) }
 return object
}
// checkedJSApply is the dispatch boundary for an already-built argument array.
// The caller owns that ordinary native array and all referenced values. It must
// finish argument construction and native probes before its final authority
// fence, then call this helper without a new getter/builder step. Type checks
// here inspect Go's js.Value tags only; the SDK still has fixed-arity transport
// overhead. This does not attest an arbitrary object's Array-like behavior.
func checkedJSApply(function, receiver, arguments js.Value) js.Value {
 defer checkedJSRecover()
 if function.Type()!=js.TypeFunction||arguments.Type()!=js.TypeObject { panic(checkedJSFailure{}) }
 return checkedJSReflection.apply.Invoke(function,receiver,arguments)
}
func checkedJSConstruct(function, arguments js.Value) js.Value {
 defer checkedJSRecover()
 if function.Type()!=js.TypeFunction||arguments.Type()!=js.TypeObject { panic(checkedJSFailure{}) }
 return checkedJSReflection.construct.Invoke(function,arguments)
}
func checkedJSCall(value js.Value, method string, args ...any) js.Value {
 defer checkedJSRecover()
 function:=checkedJSReflection.get.Invoke(value,method)
 if function.Type()!=js.TypeFunction { panic(checkedJSFailure{}) }
 arguments:=checkedJSArray(args)
 return checkedJSApply(function,value,arguments)
}
func checkedJSInvoke(function js.Value, args ...any) js.Value {
 defer checkedJSRecover()
 if function.Type()!=js.TypeFunction { panic(checkedJSFailure{}) }
 arguments:=checkedJSArray(args)
 return checkedJSApply(function,js.Undefined(),arguments)
}
func checkedJSNew(function js.Value, args ...any) js.Value {
 defer checkedJSRecover()
 if function.Type()!=js.TypeFunction { panic(checkedJSFailure{}) }
 arguments:=checkedJSArray(args)
 return checkedJSConstruct(function,arguments)
}
